objectives: Identify shared rimes in taught cr-words and familiar partner words.
Sort words by vowel-and-ending patterns rather than onset alone.
Decode every word fully after sorting.
Use controlled word groups to read a short, accurate line.
concepts: A rime includes the vowel and the sounds that follow it.
Words can share cr but have different rimes.
Words with different onsets can share a rime.
Sorting helps reading only when the whole word is decoded.

definitions.definition: The vowel and sounds that follow it in a syllable.
A group of words sharing a rime, such as crab and grab (-ab).
The consonant or consonant blend before the vowel.

workedExamples.solution: They share -ab but have different onsets.
They share -op even though the onsets differ.

commonMistakes: Grouping all cr-words together despite different rimes.
Sorting only by the first two letters.
Guessing from rhyme without decoding the full word.
keyTakeaways: Compare the vowel and ending to find a rime.
The same onset does not guarantee the same word family.
Different onsets can share a rime.
revisionPoints: Sort by rime, then read each whole word.

Try a fresh item without looking at the answer.
